verbum, verbī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

Ūnō verbō, in a word (Cic. Fin. 2.73); ad verbum, word for word (Cic. Fin. 1.4); meīs verbīs, from me, in my name (Cic. Att. 16.11.8). For verba dare see word, promise.

Other words

  • vocābulum, vocābulī n. — a word as the name of a thing

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Gell. 4.1.18: rem nōn suō vocābulō dēmōnstrāre; M-O s.v. term · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: “an appellation, designation, name of any thing”.

  • vōx, vōcis f. — a word as spoken, a saying; voice

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.6 (Lewis & Short): quid sonet haec vōx voluptātis · Declension on Wiktionary

  • dictiō, dictiōnis f. — a word (in grammar)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Quint. 1.5.2: quam vītantēs ambiguitātem quīdam dīcere māluērunt vōcēs, locūtiōnēs, dictiōnēs; Prisc. II p. 51 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 231, 249, 408 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Because verbum is both any word and the verb, Quintilian reports, some grammarians preferred to call words vōcēs, locūtiōnēs, dictiōnēs. Elsewhere classical dictiō is a saying or a way of putting things; Priscian uses it for a word. Traupman: syllabae faciunt dictiōnēs, syllables form words (249).

Examples

  • jam satis est. … verbum nōn amplius addam

    That’s enough now. … I won’t add another word.Hor. S. 1.1.120–121

  • nōndum prīma verba exprimit, jam coccum intellegit, jam conchȳlium poscit.

    He can’t say his first words yet, but he already knows scarlet and asks for purple.Quint. 1.2.6

  • hās prīmum audiet puer, hārum verba effingere imitandō cōnābitur

    these the child will hear first, and theirs are the words he will try to copyQuint. 1.1.5

  • Bona verba, quaesō.

    Don’t say such things, please!Ter. And. 204

  • exīstimātiō, dēdecus, īnfāmia verba sunt atque ineptiae

    reputation, disgrace, infamy: mere words and nonsenseCic. Pis. 65 (Lewis & Short)

  • Verba istaec sunt.

    That’s mere talk.Traupman 109

  • Nūllum verbum ēmīsit.

    She never uttered a word.Traupman 110

  • verbum prō verbō reddere

    to render word for wordCic. Opt. Gen. 14 (Lewis & Short s.v. verbum)

  • breviter, ad summam

    in a wordTraupman 408

  • Syllabae faciunt dictiōnēs.

    Syllables form words.Traupman 408

  • Cūr tibi crēdam?

    Why should I take your word for it?Traupman 408

  • verbum prō verbō

    word for wordTraupman 408

  • Mihi verba dēsunt.

    Words fail me.Traupman 408

  • Tū quidem ex ōre ōrātiōnem mihi ēripuistī.

    You took the words right out of my mouth.Traupman 408
